name: Eclipse Ditto
what_it_is: Eclipse Ditto is an open-source IoT framework implementing the digital twins pattern, providing virtual cloud-based representations of physical devices via REST, WebSocket, MQTT, AMQP, and Kafka APIs. It manages device state, access control, and search across connected things using a microservices architecture backed by MongoDB.
components: Connectivity (device connection handling for MQTT, AMQP, Kafka, HTTP)
measurement: Thing state (attributes and features of a digital twin)
configuration: JWT issuer and public key for token validation
Connectivity targets (MQTT broker, AMQP endpoint, Kafka brokers)
JVM heap and memory settings per microservice
constraints: Requires MongoDB as the mandatory persistence backend — no alternative database support documented
Requires JVM 17+ for all microservices — not a native binary
Default Docker Compose setup uses basic auth via nginx and is not production-grade for security
No built-in message broker — external MQTT broker, AMQP broker, or Kafka cluster must be provided separately for device connectivity
No direct device drivers — physical devices must connect via supported protocol endpoints
notable_absences: No built-in message broker (MQTT broker, Kafka, or AMQP broker must be supplied externally)
No built-in time-series storage for telemetry history
No high-availability or clustering configuration in default setup
No built-in dashboarding beyond the Ditto Explorer UI (no Grafana, no metrics pipeline)
